title: Book: Think and Grow Rich — Napoleon Hill (1937)
publisher: Artha Kavach original summary of a book's ideas (paraphrase, not a quotation; the author's opinion, not settled fact) — pending manual verification
text: Napoleon Hill's best-seller claims that wealth begins with a burning desire, a definite plan and persistence, and lays out thirteen principles including faith, specialised knowledge, imagination, decision and the 'mastermind' group. It was written after, he says, years of interviews with successful people of the time. It is motivational and widely read. Criticisms matter: the evidence is anecdotal, there is little verifiable research behind its claims, and 'thinking' or 'willing' wealth into existence ignores luck, opportunity and sound money management. A fair way to use it is as motivation to set goals and persist, while pairing it with budgeting, insurance, an emergency fund and diversified investing.
